findings.why_wrong: Rule 107.3.a: every Battlefield is associated with a Facedown sub-zone. Rule 811.1.b (Hidden): during an Open state on your turn you may pay [A] to hide the card at a battlefield you control. Player-1 controls Back-Alley Bar (controller=player-1), holds Blastcone Fae (has Hidden), and has 2 Mind power to pay [rainbow] — the hide is legal and the engine itself enumerated it in moves[]. Execution then fails because the production game-setup never registers the facedown-<bfId> zone (createFacedownZone in zones/zone-configs.ts has zero production callers; only testing/playtest/game-setup.ts:347 creates them). Move enumeration and executor disagree on a rules-mandated zone.
findings.reason: Trace step 20→21: moves[] enumerates hideCard{battlefieldId:player-2-bf-ogn-277-298, cardId:player-1-main-1-ogn-097-298}; player-1 controls that bf and has mind:2; Blastcone Fae has [Hidden]. After the click, state is byte-identical (zero diff keys) and the card is still in handIds — the reducer failed. Root cause: production setup at server.ts:1098 and :1184 registers only internal.zones[`battlefield-${bfCardId}`] and never a `facedown-${bfCardId}` zone; createFacedownZone (zone-configs.ts:181) has no callers anywhere; only testing/playtest/game-setup.ts:347 creates facedown zones. Enumeration passes because getCardsInZone (core/operations-impl.ts:154-158) returns [] for a missing zone, so cards.ts:1241 sees capacity available; the reducer at cards.ts:1265-1269 then calls zones.moveCard({targetZoneId:"facedown-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298"}) and core/operations-impl.ts:205-207 throws `Target zone facedown-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298 does not exist`. Rules 107.3.a and 811.1.b confirm the hide was legal and the facedown sub-zone is mandated per battlefield. (Minor: trace.json errs[] is empty so the literal error string is not captured client-side, but the source line and the no-op state transition prove the failure path.)

findings.what: Player clicked the offered 'Hide Card at Back-Alley Bar' action for Blastcone Fae; server rejected it with toast 'Move rejected: Target zone facedown-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298 does not exist'. findings.why_wrong: Rule 811.1.b / 421.2.a: a player with a Hidden card in hand may pay [A] to hide it facedown at a battlefield they control. Player-1 controls Back-Alley Bar, has Blastcone Fae ([Hidden]) in hand, and has 2 Mind power to pay — this is a legal Discretionary Action and must succeed. Root cause: apps/riftbound-app/server.ts:1098 and :1184 register only `battlefield-${bfCardId}` dynamic zones after placeBattlefields and omit the paired `facedown-${bfCardId}` zone (createFacedownZone in zone-configs.ts is exported but never called in production; only testing/playtest/game-setup.ts:347 creates it). hideCard's condition() passes because getCardsInZone on a nonexistent zone returns [], but the executor's zones.moveCard hits core operations-impl.ts:207 and throws. Net effect: the Hidden keyword is completely non-functional in real games — an enumerated legal move is unexecutable.
findings.reason: Rule 811.1.b/421.2.a verified via rule.ts. Trace step 22: player-1 controls player-2-bf-ogn-277-298 (Back-Alley Bar), has Blastcone Fae ogn-097-298 [Hidden] in hand, mind:2; hideCard is enumerated in moves[]. Step 22→23: runePools/battlefields/handIds/bfZones/moves all byte-identical, hideCard still offered. The reducer (cards.ts:1265-1268) then calls zones.moveCard to `facedown-player-2-bf-ogn-277-298`, hitting core operations-impl.ts:207 `throw new Error(`Target zone ${targetZoneId} does not exist`)`. server.ts:2968-2974 emits move_rejected with that error; websocket.js:112 renders `Move rejected: ${msg.error}` — matching the claimed toast. Hidden keyword is unexecutable in real games.

findings.what: The Recruit token created by Herald of the Arcane's ability entered player-1's base with exhausted=false (state: base[0].exhausted=false, dom.baseExhausted=0; AFTER screenshot shows the token upright, not rotated). As a direct consequence the engine is now offering standardMove for this token to both battlefields.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 143.4: 'Units enter the Board exhausted.' Rule 185.2.d explicitly restates this for tokens: 'A token unit is a unit. It enters exhausted.' Herald of the Arcane (ogn-265-298) reads '[1], [Exhaust]: Play a 1 [Might] Recruit unit token' with no 'ready' modifier and no Accelerate, so the default applies. Because the token should be exhausted, it cannot pay the Standard Move cost (rule 144.2 + 414.4: exhaust is the cost and an already-exhausted object cannot be exhausted again), so the two standardMove entries in moves[] are illegal offers.
findings.reason: Rules 143.4 and 185.2.d verified via rule.ts: token units enter exhausted. Herald of the Arcane (herald-of-the-arcane.ts:16-25) declares a plain create-token effect with no ready modifier. The create-token resolver at /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:873-909 calls ctx.createCardInZone(tokenId, ...) at :894 and registers the definition at :900-906 but never calls counters.setFlag(tokenId, "exhausted", true). The createCardInZone wrapper (chain-moves.ts:95-104) and the core impl (operations-impl.ts:40-60) also set no flags. Contrast the playUnit path at cards.ts:728-738 which does set exhausted=true per 143.4. Trace step 8 confirms base[0].exhausted=false, dom.baseExhausted=0, and moves[] contains two standardMove entries for token-recruit-1785949906006-0; movement.ts:174/241/434 gate standardMove on getFlag(unitId,"exhausted"), so the unset flag yields the illegal offers per 144.2/414.4.

findings.what: The created token's game object carries no card definition: def is set to its own instance id ('token-recruit-1785949906006-0'), name is the raw id, type='unknown', and there is no might field. UI renders a placeholder card labeled 'token-recruit-1785949906006-0 / UNKNOWN' in base and the hover panel shows a broken-image alt text; a new 404 console error fired (art lookup for the bogus def id).
findings.why_wrong: Rule 187.1: 'A 1 [M] Recruit token is a domainless unit token with 1 Might and the Recruit tag.' The chain item correctly carried {name:'Recruit', type:'unit', might:1} from TOKEN_PRESETS.RECRUIT, but the create-token resolution did not transfer that preset into the materialized game object — it minted an id and reused it as the def-id, so registry lookup fails. With type='unknown' and no might, downstream unit rules (combat damage, lethal check 143.2.a) cannot evaluate correctly.
findings.reason: Trace step 8 base[0] is exactly {id:"token-recruit-1785949906006-0", def:"token-recruit-1785949906006-0", name:"token-recruit-1785949906006-0", type:"unknown"} with no might, and errs gained a second 404. Source chain: effect-executor.ts:893 mints tokenId=`token-${slug}-${Date.now()}-${i}` and calls ctx.createCardInZone(tokenId,...); chain-moves.ts:100 wraps that call with `definitionId: cardId` so the card instance's definitionId IS its own instance id. The effect executor registers the preset in the engine's getGlobalCardRegistry() (effect-executor.ts:900-906), but the server snapshot at server.ts:663 looks up via `registry` = getCardRegistry() (server.ts:114, imported from @tcg/riftbound-cards — a static Map of set-printed cards only, all-cards.ts:899). That Map has no `token-recruit-…` key, so def is undefined and the fallbacks fire: server.ts:673 cardType→"unknown", :675 definitionId→tokenId, :680 might→undefined, :681 name→cardId. Rule 187.1 confirms a Recruit token must be a unit with 1 Might; the materialized snapshot object carries neither.

findings.what: Recycling the Mind Rune triggered a console 404 ("Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404") that was not present at step 9.
findings.why_wrong: DESIGN.md requires all card/asset images preloaded with no failed loads during play; the harness flags this as invariant `no-console-errors`. Not a rules violation — the recycle itself resolved correctly per rule 164.2.b / 416.1.b — but an asset request tied to the recycle action failed.
findings.reason: Trace confirms a 404 console error at step 10 (errs=["[console] Failed to load resource... 404"], invariantViolations=[no-console-errors]) and none at step 9. However, the failing asset is NOT tied to the recycle mechanic itself — it is the Recruit token's card image. Root cause chain: effect-executor.ts:893 mints tokenId="token-recruit-1785949906006-0"; chain-moves.ts:100 sets `definitionId: cardId` (so the token's definitionId is its timestamped instance id, not a stable `token-def-recruit` slug); renderer.js:629+666 emit ``; server.ts:2349-2370 finds no local file and no cardImageUrls entry (only `token-def-${slug}` is indexed at server.ts:132) and returns 404. Step 9 (menu-expand click, no move) triggers no re-render; step 10's recycleRune execution triggers renderZones(), re-creating the token's `` and re-firing the 404. The same 404 also appears at steps 7, 8, 11, 13, 14 — every board re-render while the token is present — so the bug is the ability-path token definitionId, not anything recycle-specific. Invariant flag at monkey-drive.ts:149.

findings.what: The Recruit token is on the board with def-id equal to its instance id ('token-recruit-1785949906006-0'), name = raw id, type='unknown', and no might field. On this step it also produced a console 404 (card art fetch by the bad def-id) and renders as a grey 'UNKNOWN' placeholder.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 185.2.d: a token unit is a unit — it enters exhausted, has Might, deals damage equal to its Might in combat, etc. A Recruit token must have type=unit and might=1. With type=unknown/no might, the upcoming conquer/combat resolution at Back-Alley Bar will compute wrong damage, and the client cannot render the card. The token-creation path assigned the instance id as the card definition id instead of a real Recruit token def.
findings.reason: Trace step 12 base[0] shows {id:"token-recruit-1785949906006-0", def:"token-recruit-1785949906006-0", name:"token-recruit-1785949906006-0", type:"unknown", exhausted:false, damage:0} with no might; step 13 errs=["[console] Failed to load resource: ... 404 ..."]. Root cause: chain-moves.ts:100 sets `definitionId: cardId` (instance id as def id) when adapting the effect-executor createCardInZone call; effect-executor.ts:900-906 registers the token def under that tokenId in getGlobalCardRegistry(), but server.ts:114 uses `getCardRegistry()` from @tcg/riftbound-cards (static card map, all-cards.ts:899), so server.ts:663 `registry.get(cardInstance.definitionId)` returns undefined → server.ts:673 cardType="unknown", :680 might=undefined, :681 name=cardId. renderer.js:666 fetches `/card-image/${imgId}` by that bad def-id → 404, and onerror at :667-672 shows the .card-fallback placeholder with fallback-type text "unknown". Rule 185.2.d requires token units to have Might and be type=unit; this token has neither, so combat/conquer at Back-Alley Bar will compute wrong damage.

findings.what: After the non-combat showdown closed and player-1 established control of Back-Alley Bar, the engine left the battlefield as {contested: true, contestedBy: 'player-1', showdownComplete: false}. Consequently `startShowdown` is re-enumerated as a legal move on a battlefield the player already controls and just conquered (visible in step-14 moves[] and the 'Start Showdown — Back-Alley Bar' button in the AFTER screenshot).
findings.why_wrong: Rule 190.3.b: a battlefield 'remains Contested until Control is established or re-established' — control WAS established here (348.2.a), so Contested must clear (combat's 466.5.a does this explicitly). Rule 344/190.3.a.1: a Showdown only opens when a player who does NOT control the battlefield contests it; player-1 now controls it and is the only one with units there, so no showdown can be staged. The passShowdownFocus reducer's non-combat branch (chain-moves.ts:1075-1108) sets bf.controller and awards VP but never clears bf.contested nor sets bf.showdownComplete=true (only the combat branch at :1074 does), so the startShowdown enumerator (:1172) keeps offering it forever.
findings.reason: Trace step 14 (after passShowdownFocus on non-combat showdown): battlefields.player-2-bf-ogn-277-298 = {contested:true, controller:"player-1", contestedBy:"player-1", showdownComplete:false}; moves[] includes {moveId:"startShowdown", battlefieldId:"player-2-bf-ogn-277-298"}; dom.actionButtons includes "Start Showdown Back-Alley Bar". Source: chain-moves.ts:1072-1074 combat branch sets bf.showdownComplete=true, but the non-combat else-branch (:1075-1108) only sets bf.controller=solo (:1088) and awards VP — never clears bf.contested nor sets bf.showdownComplete. startShowdown enumerator at :1172 gates on `bf?.contested && !bf.showdownComplete`, so it re-offers the just-conquered battlefield. Rules 348.2.a (control established) + 190.3.b (contested clears once control established) + 344 (showdown requires genuine contest) confirm this is wrong.

findings.what: The Recruit token is served to the client with its generated instance id as its definition id (def: 'token-recruit-1785949906006-0', name: same, type: 'unknown'), causing 404s on the card-definition fetch (console errors in errs[]) and a blank card render in the battlefield slot.
findings.why_wrong: Rule 187.1 defines the '1 [M] Recruit token' as a real domainless unit with 1 Might and the Recruit tag. The token should reference a stable Recruit card definition so the client can render name/art/might; instead the per-instance timestamped id is used as the def id, which the card server cannot resolve. This is why the AFTER screenshot shows an empty box instead of a Recruit card, and likely why the exhausted rotation also fails (renderer bails on unknown type).
findings.reason: Trace step 13 bfZones shows {id:'token-recruit-1785949906006-0', def:same, name:same, type:'unknown', exhausted:true} plus a 404 console error and exhausted-rendered invariant violation. Root cause: the chain-effect token path mints tokenId with Date.now() (effect-executor.ts:893) and the chain-moves bridge stores it as the card's definitionId — chain-moves.ts:100 `definitionId: cardId`. Contrast token.ts:131 which correctly uses stable `token-def-recruit`. Server serialization (server.ts:663) then does registry.get(cardInstance.definitionId) against the static getCardRegistry() map (server.ts:114), which has no `token-recruit--0` entry, so def is undefined → cardType:'unknown' (server.ts:673), definitionId: (server.ts:675), name:cardId (server.ts:681). Client renderer.js:628-629,666 builds ``; the /card-image/ route only indexed `token-def-recruit` (server.ts:132-133) → 404. Rule 187.1 confirms Recruit is a real 1-Might domainless unit that should have a resolvable definition.

findings.expected: Per the ruling: casting Thrill of the Hunt banishes the friendly unit, then adds it to the chain as a pending item [354.2]; when the spell finishes resolving, Abandoned Hall's play-spell trigger becomes pending AFTER the unit [419.4.a/383.2.c]; pending items finalize in append order [337.1.b], so the unit resolves and lands at Abandoned Hall first; the trigger then finalizes and the replayed unit is a valid choice for the +1 Might buff.
findings.observed: Set up goldfish game (Abandoned Hall = battlefield-player-1-bf-unl-205-219). Played Legion Rearguard to base, then cast Thrill of the Hunt (unl-184-219) and passed priority. Result: Legion Rearguard was moved to the banishment zone and stayed there — it was never replayed to any battlefield. Abandoned Hall's triggered ability never fired: interaction.nextChainItemId=2 after full resolution, i.e. only the spell (chain-1) was ever placed on the chain; no unit chain-item and no triggered-ability chain-item were created. No target-choice prompt was offered. bfZones for Abandoned Hall remained empty. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-a92fdaf27c81161c.png.
findings.notes: Two independent engine defects block this ruling: (1) Card-data parse bug — unl-205-219's ability has trigger:{event:'play-spell', on:'self'}; trigger-matcher.ts:164-168 rejects on:'self' when event.cardId (the spell) != card.id (the battlefield), so Abandoned Hall's trigger can never match ANY spell. Rules text is 'When a player plays a spell', which should parse as on:'any-player' (or similar). (2) Replay stub — effect-executor.ts:1062-1074 case 'play' just moves resolved targets to base; it does not resolve target:{type:'pending-value'} (so getTargetIds returned nothing and the banished unit stayed in banishment), does not honor toLocation:{battlefield:'any'}, and does not add the replayed card to the chain per rule 354.2/354.3. Even if (1) were fixed, the engine would still not present the replayed unit at Abandoned Hall when the trigger's target is chosen. Files: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts (L162-178), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts (L1062-1074), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/chain-moves.ts (L237-262 — play-spell fires after executeEffect, ordering itself would be OK if the two bugs above were fixed), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/data/sets/unl.json (unl-205-219 abilities[0].trigger.on).

findings.expected: Per the ruling: playing Akshan with the [body][body] additional cost moves an enemy gear to your base and creates a 'you control it until I leave the board' continuous effect. With two Akshans on the same gear, timestamp ordering (rules 478/480) means the most-recently-played Akshan's controller controls the gear; when one Akshan dies its effect ends and the surviving Akshan's effect (or original owner) determines control.
findings.observed: Akshan's ability does not fire at all. Played player-1 Akshan with paidAdditionalCost:true against player-2's Hunter's Machete (unl-096-219) in base: energy dropped 15→11 (base cost only), body power stayed at 6 (additional cost NOT deducted), machete remained controller=player-2 owner=player-2 in p2's base, not moved and not attached to Akshan. No pendingChoice, no chain item, no continuousEffects entry. Move enumerator offers only {cardId, location, playerId} for Akshan — no paidAdditionalCost variant.
findings.notes: Root cause: getOptionalPlayCost() in packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:113-129 only recognizes Accelerate keyword and 'kill a friendly X' additional-cost patterns. Akshan's parsed ability ({type:'static', effect:{type:'additional-cost-option', additionalCost:'[body][body]'}} from parser/index.ts:4737-4748) is not matched, so optional=undefined and paidAdditionalCostActual stays false; the play-self event fires with paidAdditionalCost:false and the 'if you paid' trigger condition (trigger-runner.ts:127) fails. Additionally, grep found no timestamp-ordered continuous-effect / control-layer infrastructure (rules 477/478/480) in riftbound-engine — card.controller is a plain field, not computed via layered effects — so even if the trigger fired, the two-Akshan layered-control resolution the ruling describes has no engine support. The layered-control question is therefore unreachable; the base ability being non-functional is the reportable divergence. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-daad578f2f4573e0.png

findings.expected: Per ruling: when finalizing Alpha Strike on the chain, the caster (1) explicitly chooses a friendly unit as a standard target, then (2) chooses UP TO N enemy units at battlefields as split targets, where N = the friendly unit's current Might; the caster MAY choose fewer than N, including zero; all choices lock at finalization. Implication: with a friendly unit on board and zero enemy units, Alpha Strike is legally playable (choose friendly unit, choose zero split targets).
findings.observed: Engine offers no target choices at all and rejects the play. With a friendly Legion Rearguard (might 2) at base and zero enemy units, `playSpell` for Alpha Strike is not enumerated (0 moves offered) and direct execution returns CONDITION_FAILED. Root causes in code: (a) the card def encodes the friendly-unit choice as `amount:{might:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}}`, but resolveAmount() in effect-executor.ts:167-224 only handles `might:'self'` (string) — this descriptor form falls through to `return 0`, so no friendly unit is ever chosen and the damage amount is always 0; (b) the split targets are declared `{quantity:'all', split:true}` — the playSpell enumerator (cards.ts:1067-1092) treats quantity:'all' as programmatic, so no per-enemy-unit selection is offered; the `split:true` flag is never read anywhere in the engine (grep confirms no consumer); (c) spellEffectHasLegalTargets() gates the sequence's for-each sub-effect on its `filter:'damaged'` target, so Alpha Strike is unplayable unless a damaged enemy unit already exists at a battlefield — contradicting the ruling that zero split targets is legal. Net: the engine implements neither the 'choose a friendly unit' step nor the 'choose up to N enemy units (may choose fewer)' step.
findings.notes: Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-6b3effc73787ce91.png. Card def: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts. Engine paths: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts (resolveAmount + damage case, no split handling), /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:413-477 (spellEffectHasLegalTargets gate) and :1063-1092 (target enumeration only for single top-level card targets). Also attempted setup with 4 enemy Recruit tokens + 1 enemy Mech at battlefield-player-2; Alpha Strike still not offered/playable (tokens are registered under definitionId not instanceId so target-resolver's registry.get() misses them, but the CONDITION_FAILED persists regardless because of the for-each filter gate).

findings.expected: Per rules 355.14.e-g / 359.3.f.2: at finalization the caster chooses a friendly unit and the set of enemy-unit targets at battlefields; at RESOLUTION the caster distributes damage equal to the friendly unit's current effective Might among those targets, each target receiving >=1, with all damage distributed. Buffs/debuffs applied between finalization and resolution change the damage pool.
findings.observed: Engine has no split-distribution mechanic at all. Live test (game d139d9db, screenshot /tmp/ruling-da6fb2fa426580ff.png): with a friendly Voracious Gromp (M5) at base and two enemy units (Demacian Diplomat M2, Shipyard Skulker M3) at a battlefield during a showdown, playSpell for Alpha Strike is rejected with CONDITION_FAILED — the play-legality gate (spellEffectHasLegalTargets) recurses into the for-each XP sub-effect and demands a pre-existing 'damaged' enemy unit at a battlefield, and the condition-path resolver ctx omits getCardMeta so filter:'damaged' can never match. Code inspection of the resolution path confirms further divergence: effect-executor.ts:375-427 ignores the `split:true` flag entirely and applies the full amount to EVERY target; resolveAmount() (lines 183-188) only handles might:'self', so Alpha Strike's amount {might:{controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}} falls through to `return 0`. There is no 'choose a friendly unit' step, no caster-chosen enemy targets (quantity:'all' auto-selects), no pendingChoice for damage distribution at resolution, and the damage pool would be 0 rather than the chosen unit's Might.
findings.notes: Relevant files: /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/unl/alpha-strike.ts (card def with split:true); /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/effect-executor.ts:375-427 (damage case ignores split), :167-224 (resolveAmount returns 0 for non-'self' might refs); /root/src/tcg/tcg-engines/packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/cards.ts:413-438 + :977-992 (spellEffectHasLegalTargets treats for-each scope as a required target and condition ctx lacks getCardMeta). Net: Alpha Strike is effectively unplayable, and even if the legality gate were bypassed, resolution would deal 0 damage to every enemy unit with no distribution choice — diverging from every clause of the ruling (355.14.e/f/g and 359.3.f.2).

findings.expected: Alpha Strike is playable by choosing a friendly unit and N enemy-unit targets; if the friendly unit's might is reduced between finalization and resolution to M < N, the controller must drop exactly (N - M) targets so the remaining target count equals M, and may not drop more than that to concentrate damage [355.14.h / 355.14.h.1].
findings.observed: Alpha Strike cannot be played at all. With a friendly 3-might Noxus Saboteur on one battlefield and three enemy 3-might Noxus Saboteurs (one pre-damaged) on another, executeMove('playSpell', {cardId: alpha-strike}) returns {success:false, error:"Move 'playSpell' condition not met", errorCode:"CONDITION_FAILED"}. Root cause: spellEffectHasLegalTargets (cards.ts:413) recurses into the sequence's second sub-effect (for-each over enemy units with filter:'damaged'); the legality-check context (cards.ts:978-989) omits getCardMeta, so matchesFilter('damaged') (target-resolver.ts:222-223) always evaluates (undefined?.damage ?? 0) > 0 = false, yielding an empty target set and failing the >0 gate. Beyond the play gate, the mechanic under test is not implemented: (a) the 'damage' effect executor (effect-executor.ts:375-427) ignores split:true and applies the full amount to every target with no distribution step; (b) resolveAmount (effect-executor.ts:183-188) handles only might:'self', not the target-descriptor form {controller:'friendly',type:'unit'}, so Alpha Strike's amount would resolve to 0; (c) no code path anywhere implements 355.14.h target-dropping (grep for 'cease.*target|dropTarget|355.14' in riftbound-engine finds nothing).
findings.notes: Board set up via /api/game/:id/tutor + duplicateCard sandbox move (real Noxus Saboteur ogn-018-298 instances, registry-registered, owner=player-2 for enemies). addToken tokens are unusable for this test — they register only under definitionId, not instance ID, so resolveTarget's cardType filter drops them. The card definition itself (alpha-strike.ts) already carries a FIXME acknowledging the for-each is an approximation. The might-reduction reaction step could not be reached because the spell never gets onto the chain; even if it could, the split/target-drop logic to verify the ruling against is absent. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-013355072ffd6542.png

findings.expected: When Svellsongur (sfd-059-221) is attached to Aphelios, Exalted (sfd-049-221), Aphelios's 'When you attach an Equipment to me' triggered ability fires exactly once — one modal choice (Ready 2 runes / Channel 1 rune exhausted / Buff a friendly unit) is put on the chain. Not zero, not twice.
findings.observed: Zero triggers. After executing equipCard(Svellsongur → Aphelios), Svellsongur correctly attached (meta.attachedTo + copiedFromCardId set, Aphelios meta.equippedWith populated), but the chain remained empty, no interaction/choice prompt appeared, the game log recorded only 'dev: equip card', and rune state was unchanged. Aphelios's ability never fired.
findings.notes: Root cause: the attach-equipment trigger event is not wired up in the engine. (1) packages/riftbound-engine/src/game-definition/moves/equipment.ts equipCard.execute() updates card meta but emits no game event. (2) packages/riftbound-engine/src/abilities/trigger-matcher.ts EVENT_MAP has no 'attach-equipment' entry. Aphelios's card def (packages/riftbound-cards/src/cards/sfd/aphelios-exalted.ts) uses trigger.event='attach-equipment', which therefore never matches. Because the base trigger doesn't fire at all, the ruling's finer point (Svellsongur's copied text should NOT produce a second trigger) cannot be reached — but 0 triggers still diverges from the ruling's 1. Also noted: equipCard is not enumerated in `pw moves` (no Equip activated-ability move offered); had to invoke equipCard directly. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-41492fa40ce64fb4.png. Shady Spectacles sub-scenario not separately tested since it depends on the same missing attach-equipment event.

findings.expected: After Arcane Shift banishes the caster's only unit at a controlled battlefield, that unit is added to the chain as a pending item (rule 354.2); the pending item keeps the turn in a Closed State so cleanup step 323.6 does not strip control; when the pending unit finalizes, the player can choose that same battlefield as its play location and the unit re-enters there.
findings.observed: Setup: player-1 controls battlefield BF1 (Abandoned Hall) with Daring Poro as the only unit; an enemy Daring Poro copy sits at BF2 to satisfy the damage target. Cast Arcane Shift and let the chain resolve. Result: the friendly Poro is moved to the banishment zone and NEVER re-enters play — no pending chain item is created, no play-location choice is offered, and after resolution interaction.chain=null with pendingChoice=null. Because no pending item keeps the chain alive, cleanup runs in an Open State and BF1's controller flips from player-1 to null. The `play` sub-effect with target {type:'pending-value'} is not wired to the banish result: effect-executor's `sequence` handler ignores `pendingValue`, and the `play` handler unconditionally moves whatever resolveTarget returns to zone 'base' (here it grabbed the enemy unit off BF2 and dropped it into player-2's base). Final zones: banishment=[Daring Poro (player-1), Arcane Shift]; battlefield-BF1=[]; battlefields.BF1.controller=null.
findings.notes: Root cause is the effect executor, not the cleanup rule: state-based-checks.ts already gates 323.6 on !chain.active (comment even cites the banished-then-replayed case), but effect-executor.ts case 'play' (line ~1062) hard-codes targetZoneId='base' and never pushes a pending item, and case 'sequence' (line ~934) does not thread pendingValue.source into the child effect's target — so {type:'pending-value'} falls through resolveTarget as an unfiltered board scan instead of resolving to the just-banished card. Net effect: the ruling's step 2 ('added to the chain as a pending item') and step 6 ('choose where to play it — battlefield still controlled') are both unreachable in the engine. Screenshot: /tmp/ruling-ee735b43996dcbd3.png. Secondary observation (not part of this ruling): playSpell's condition gates on a legal enemy-unit-at-battlefield target for the 'Deal 3' clause, so Arcane Shift is unplayable in goldfish without seeding an enemy board unit.
